title: AWS Support Plans & Resources 📞
description: Compare support tiers and find free help when you’re stuck.

slides.title: The Four Support Plans 🏆
slides.content:
# From Free to Enterprise

- **Basic** (free): 24/7 customer service for account/billing, access to forums, documentation, and AWS Health Dashboard.
- **Developer** (starts ~$29/month): + email support with 12‑hour response time during business hours, general guidance.
- **Business** (starts ~$100/month): + phone/chat support, 1‑hour response for production‑impacting issues, infrastructure event management.
- **Enterprise** (starts ~$15,000/month): + 15‑minute response, dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM), architecture reviews.

For this course, Basic is all you need.

quizData.question: Which support plan includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM)?
quizData.explanation: Only the Enterprise plan includes a TAM who helps with architecture, reviews, and advocacy.

slides.title: Free Support Resources 📚
slides.content:
# You’re Not Alone

Even with Basic support, you have:
- **AWS Documentation**: Official guides, API references.
- **AWS re:Post**: Community Q&A (like Stack Overflow for AWS).
- **AWS Knowledge Center**: Common issues and solutions.
- **AWS Free Tier Forums**: Ask questions with no charge.
- **YouTube**: AWS Events, re:Invent sessions, this course 😉

Take advantage of these – they’re gold when you’re learning.

slides.title: AWS Health Dashboard ❤️
slides.content:
# Is AWS Down?

The **AWS Health Dashboard** (free) shows real‑time service status and any issues affecting your resources.

- **Service Health Dashboard**: Public page showing all regions.
- **Personal Health Dashboard**: Tailored to your account, shows issues specific to your resources.

Bookmark it – it’s the first place to check when something seems wrong.

slides.title: Pro Tip: AWS Trusted Advisor 🧠
slides.content:
## Free Checks

Trusted Advisor inspects your environment and makes recommendations (cost optimisation, security, fault tolerance). Basic and Developer plans get 7 core checks for free. Use them!

It’ll tell you if you have open S3 buckets, unused elastic IPs, and more.
